t: The deeper wall sounds solid, but the edge needs another support.
I struck good stone all morning and broke the handle instead.
The dust tastes different near a damp wall.
I should set another brace before anyone works beneath that ledge.
The crack widened after the last blow. I need to watch it.
My lamp smoked all morning. The wick needs trimming.
Good ore hides behind stone that looks like every other stone.
I heard loose grit before the small fall. That sound matters.
The wedge is bending. I should replace it before it traps the hammer.
Cold air is coming through that narrow crack.
I need to mark the safe path before the dust settles.
That wall gave more stone than I expected and less ore.
My shoulders know exactly how many loads came out today.
The tunnel feels smaller after a full day inside it.
Tomorrow I start where the rock changed color.
The tracks are fresh, but the animal is moving into the wind.
I waited beside the trail too long and let my feet go numb.
That print is smaller than yesterday's. There may be two animals.
The binding held, though I should tighten it before another throw.
Birds went quiet ahead of me. Something else was already there.
I found hair on the bark but no blood on the ground.
The trail crossed water and vanished exactly where I expected.
I should approach from the other ridge tomorrow.
An empty hunt still tells me where not to wait again.
The wind turned at the worst moment and gave me away.
Fresh droppings, broken grass, and still no animal in sight.
I need a quieter strap before I go out again.
The ground is soft enough to read every step today.
I saw the animal first, but it heard me second.
Tomorrow I will wait longer before deciding nothing is coming.
The shaded bushes still have fruit after the sunny ones are bare.
I should bring a smaller basket for the narrow path.
Half the berries looked ripe until I reached them.
The best patch is always one hill farther than I want.
I found nuts where the ground stays dry beneath the trees.
My fingers are stained enough to prove where I have been.
The birds left one branch untouched. I should remember why.
I picked the easy fruit first and saved my knees.
That patch needs two more days before anyone touches it.
A full basket makes every slope feel steeper.
I should leave some fruit for seed and some for the birds.
The damp ground keeps the roots easy to pull.
I know three good patches and trust none of them after frost.
The basket handle bites harder when the village is still far away.
Tomorrow I will start near the creek before others reach it.
People ask for certainty when what they need is somebody to listen.
I should remember that silence can be part of an answer.
The shrine needs sweeping before anyone arrives tomorrow.
I spoke too long today and answered less than I should have.
One honest doubt is better than a dozen borrowed declarations.
I need to visit the family who stopped coming.
People watch my face when the god does something frightening.
I should ask who needs help before choosing tonight's story.
The doubter in the back listened longer than the believer in front.
A prayer remembered badly can become a promise nobody made.
The god sees these empty bowls. Help must be coming.
I will endure this hunger. The god has not forgotten us.
The stores are thin, but providence has found us before.
I should share what remains and trust the god with tomorrow.
Hunger tests faith more honestly than a full table does.
The god fed us once. I will remember that before complaining.
My stomach is loud, but my trust can be louder.
I will eat after the children and call that service.
Maybe the god knows we are hungry. Knowing is not feeding.
An empty stomach makes every belief feel less certain.
I prayed for food yesterday. Today the bowl is still empty.
Help may be coming, but hunger has already arrived.
I want to trust. I also want something solid to chew.
Perhaps the god is testing us. Perhaps the stores are simply bare.
Faith is difficult when supper depends on an answer.
I keep looking toward the shrine and then toward the storehouse.
The god cannot fill a storehouse that nobody works to fill.
Prayer will not thicken this stew. More food will.
My stomach needs grain, not another explanation.
People thank the god when workers finally bring food home.
The stores are empty because supplies are low, not because faith is.
I will help find supper before I kneel for it.
Hunger is a problem for hands, fields, and hunters.
A full bowl will persuade me faster than a full shrine.
You know our need. Please fill these bowls before another night passes.
We have shared the last scraps. Send enough that kindness can continue.
Feed the children first. The rest of us can wait a little longer.
If you hear this, we need food more than a sign.
I am asking again because the hunger did not leave.
Help us find enough to stop counting every mouthful.
I do not expect an answer, but hungry people try every door.
If you are real, food would be more useful than mystery.
I came because somebody should ask. I still trust the workers more.
